ratings.reviewer_notes: Caffeine inhibits telomeric DNA synthesis in telomerase-independent ALT tumor cells; it does not test telomerase activation in human immune cells.
Tests caffeic acid undecyl ester, not caffeine, and reports inhibition rather than activation of telomerase in a B-cell leukemia line.
Uses caffeine to inhibit ATR signaling in telomerase-immortalized human fibroblasts but does not assess caffeine-induced telomerase activation or immune cells.
Human cross-sectional evidence links caffeine intake to shorter leukocyte telomeres, but it neither measures telomerase activity nor establishes causality.
Directly tests caffeine uptake and signaling effects in human myeloid immune cells, including monocytes and basophils, but does not measure TERT expression or telomerase activation.
Review concerns EGCG effects, including telomerase inhibition, in glioma; it does not test caffeine or human immune cells.
Examines vascular endothelial senescence, with caffeine used as an ATM blocker; the abstract does not demonstrate caffeine-driven telomerase activation and the cells are not immune cells.
Caffeine reversal of a checkpoint and telomerase-mediated rescue are separate observations; no causal caffeine-to-telomerase link is tested, and the model is fibroblasts.
Studies polyphenols from a low-caffeine tea and their anticancer targets, not caffeine-induced telomerase activation in human immune cells.
Broad review of possible green-tea cancer-preventive mechanisms; the abstract provides no evidence connecting caffeine to telomerase activation in human immune cells.

Provides direct causal evidence that caffeine increases TERT expression and TERT-dependent telomere elongation, but the abstract does not identify the cellular model as human immune cells; in vivo evidence is from mouse thymus and spleen.
